title: Folio 4: The Judge Who Lied to Save a Life | The Honest Historian – Stories from Beyhaqi
description:
A man sits blindfolded on the executioner's mat, and the sword is already drawn. In the middle of the night, the chief judge of the Abbasid empire rides to stop it, armed with nothing but words. This is the story of Afshin, Bu Dulaf and Ahmad ibn Abi Duwad, as Beyhaqi tells it.

0:00 Cold open
0:15 Welcome
0:53 A story within a story
1:47 Three men
3:12 Midnight
4:20 The caliph's slip
5:40 The leather mat
6:41 A thousand kisses
8:09 The message
9:30 It is my message
10:49 The judge's answer
11:45 Great men
12:37 Why here?
13:31 Next week

Source: Tarikh-e Beyhaqi, the story of Afshin and the deliverance of Bu Dulaf (told before the hanging of Hasanak, after Ismail ibn Shihab from Ahmad ibn Abi Duwad); with standard scholarship for Afshin's background and his trial and death (840-841 CE).
Retold in English from the Persian original by Mehdi Rahmani and narrated with an AI rendering of his own voice.

Listen on Spotify, Apple Podcasts and every podcast app: https://mehdimrahmani.github.io/kalila-videos/podcast/
